text: The 25 LOV-REF-TABLE values of v4 are copied unchanged and the twelve codes of RWB-P3-E1043-CON are read as the subset the contract names; the list is not shortened in this workbook and the reference data administrator reconciles the two sets before the first approved load in wave 1.
why: The v4 workbook and the realignment contract story disagree on how many table codes LOV-REF-TABLE carries, and root rule 1 keeps every value of the source; the contract is the target reading of the load surface, not of the catalogue.
read: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx sheets Lists (row LOV-REF-TABLE) and Values (25 LOV-REF-TABLE rows); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-P3 rwb-case (Case and workflow)/RWB P3 E1043 CON Reference data service with versioned tables - contract v1.md sections 3, 7 AC1 and 12.7; Template and Rules section R3 (source precedence) and R9.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v5.xlsx (Lists, Values and Reference data starter sheets)
confirm: Reference data administrator and the rwb-case service owner confirm the twelve codes at the reference-data design review of wave 1.
impact: No value is lost from the catalogue; the contract serves eleven of the twelve codes it names and the rwb-access DoA operation serves the twelfth.

text: LOV-MATCH-TYPE is held by P7 rwb-decision as a decision-table column of the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package and read by P8 rwb-payment, because payment_match_rule is dropped in the target and has no Ownership Map row.
why: The v4 'Used by' cell names a table that no longer exists in the target; ADR-012 replaces it with a rule package column, and the rule package registry is P7 under the R-PREC default ruling.
read: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3.md ADR-012 decision bullet on payment_match_rule; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx sheets Tables and Rulings; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slide 41 (P7 DMN model registry) and slide 44 (JOB-07 in rwb-payment); Template and Rules section R3 (rule package registry, P7).
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v5.xlsx (Lists row LOV-MATCH-TYPE; Reference data starter rows for P8)
confirm: Center of excellence confirms that the three match-type codes travel with the PAYMENT_MATCH package at the wave 2 rule review.
impact: The three values stay in the Values sheet and are read through the rwb-decision package rather than a payment table; the decision log records the package version.

text: S1 rwb-valuation and S7 rwb-writeoff read the shared lists through the contracts of their holders on the same terms as every other consumer, and their starter rows are left open rather than derived from an unnamed list.
why: The derivation needs a table the service owns and a list the table's column uses; neither service has both, so a row would be invented.
read: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx sheet Tables (93 rows, no S1 row, write_off for S7) and sheet Services (wave 3 for S1, wave 4 for S7); 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx sheet Lists column 'Used by'.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v5.xlsx (Reference data starter, note row 4 and the Read me open points)
confirm: Service owners of S1 and S7 name the lists each reads in their own stories at the design review of their wave.
impact: The starter is complete for 17 services and the platform library and visibly open for two; no list is assigned to a service by guess.

text: A starter row exists when the service owns a table whose column uses a list, owns the ACE view a list column is read from, or owns a reference table; the service's wave from the Ownership Map is the wave it is first needed, and a list held once is read by every other service through the holder's contract.
why: The refdata starter the realignment needs has no source, so it is defined by a rule over two sources the programme already owns rather than by a new business decision.
read: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx sheet Lists columns 'Used by' and 'Source'; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx sheets Tables, Services and Rulings; Template and Rules sections R5.5 (DP-05, DP-07) and R4 (service waves).
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v5.xlsx (Reference data starter, 179 rows; Change process step 9)
confirm: Data architecture team accepts the rule, and each service story confirms its own rows at its design review.
impact: Every service has a stated Day-1 reference position; the rule is written on the sheet so a reader can recompute any row.

text: Values of a source list stay with the table that holds them after the split: rule_row in rwb_decision for LOV-DECISION, document_type and retention_rule in rwb_document for LOV-DOC-TYPE and LOV-RETENTION, and role in rwb_access for LOV-ROLE; consumers read the holder's contract, and the rwb-case list read serves lov_value, reference_row and reference_version only.
why: The split moves every table to one schema, so a list whose values come from a table moves with that table; the Ownership Map rules the four tables to P7, P5 and P4.
read: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx sheet Lists (Source cells and the header note of row 2); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx sheet Tables rows rule_row, document_type, retention_rule and role with rulings ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-tables-10; RWB P3 E1043 CON sections 12.2 and 12.7.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v5.xlsx (Lists columns G to J, rows LOV-DECISION, LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-RETENTION and LOV-ROLE)
confirm: Service owners of P4, P5 and P7 confirm the route in their contract stories of wave 1.
impact: No list is duplicated across schemas, and a consumer knows which contract to call for each of the four lists.

text: Column D keeps its stewardship owner, and the service that loads and serves the list is read from the appended 'Owning service (D-RCV-60)' and 'Owning schema (D-RCV-60)' columns; the Key sheet gains both terms.
why: The WP requires the Ownership Map for every owner, and the business owner of a value is a role that approves a change, not a schema.
read: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v4.xlsx sheets Lists column D (16 distinct roles) and Reference tables column D; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx sheets Services and Tables; Template and Rules section R9 and root rule 4 (roles only, no names).
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Reference Data and Lists of Values v5.xlsx (Lists columns G and H; Reference tables columns F and G; Key rows 13 to 16)
confirm: Data steward and data product owner confirms at the wave 1 document review that the two columns are read as stewardship and service ownership.
impact: Both owners are visible on one row and neither replaces the other; the change process keeps the approver it had.

text: The five reference-data rows that name no table take their owner from the map item behind them (timer and reference_row P3, document_type and retention_rule P5, masking_rule P4), and the message catalogue is carried in reference_row of rwb_case because the Ownership Map has no message table.
why: The Table cells of the five rows read 'Reference table', so an owner has to come from the item and the Ownership Map, and the message catalogue is versioned reference data with no table of its own in the map.
